I submit it's hard to dispute programmers in general have a subculture: "Subculture, a concept from the academic fields of sociology and cultural studies, is a group of people within a culture that differentiates itself from the parent culture to which it belongs, often maintaining some of its founding principles."
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subculture

More:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hacker_culture
https://softwareengineering.stackexchange.com/questions/12343/is-programming-a-subculture

Can this subculture be subset further such that users of a specific programming language have a subculture?
Can a programming language have a "culture" / "subculture"?

I would say so, yes. I would use gamers as an example group.

For starters, you have 'gamers', which is a subculture by itself set apart from the mainstream. Of course the last few years has shown it to be more widely embraced, if not accepted by a larger audience.

Then you have PC only gamers, and console only gamers, and those that play on both. In any case, you could point to any subs that are dedicated to one or the other. i.e. r/pcmasterrace, etc.

Further, you could look at specific game communities. For instance - WOW, COD, Battlefield, etc.

Each of these games and more have their own niche communities because they are going to talk about the game, strategies and other things that are specific to those games.

To bring it back full circle, you would most likely have discussion boards and communities specific to certain programming languages. While many do straddle the line and may participate in both, there's not much sense in talking C++ in a Python discussion; generally speaking.
